text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penis and digit).

The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures are pathognomonic for malignancy. Given the history of heavy smoking, African origin, and the specific presentation of non-healing, crusted lesions on the penis and finger, this is consistent with invasive squamous cell carcinoma. No further testing is required to confirm this diagnosis based on the provided pathology.
